As a member of the IT and Security team, this engineer supports end-user computers, mobile devices, applications, accounts, and workplace technology. They own requests through resolution, keep employees informed, and coordinate with other support engineers and specialists when an issue requires additional expertise. The ideal candidate combines strong troubleshooting skills with patient, clear communication. They can prioritize competing requests, explain technical steps in plain language, document their work, and manage the full employee and hardware lifecycle from onboarding and deployment through replacement, recovery, and offboarding. End User Support and Technical Operations Answer the IT support phone line and respond promptly to tickets, chats, and walk-up requests; provide a welcoming and reliable first point of contact. Diagnose and resolve common account, application, device, connectivity, printing, and collaboration issues during the first contact whenever practical. Provide Level 2 troubleshooting for Windows and Apple computers, mobile devices, peripherals, phone and voice services, and meeting room technology. Record symptoms, troubleshooting steps, resolution, urgency, and follow-up in the service desk system; classify and prioritize requests accurately. Own assigned incidents and requests through resolution, communicate status to employees, and escalate with clear context when specialized support is needed. Prepare, image, configure, deploy, upgrade, replace, recover, and securely retire employee devices and peripherals in accordance with IT standards. Coordinate employee onboarding, role changes, and offboarding, including account and access requests, equipment setup, collection, inventory, and documentation. Innovation Identify recurring contacts and suggest practical changes that improve first contact resolution and the employee support experience. Maintain useful knowledge articles, troubleshooting steps, and device setup instructions for the team and employees. Recommend safe workarounds that restore productivity while longer-term fixes are being developed. Help improve service desk processes, ticket quality, response times, and hardware lifecycle practices. Agility Adapt to changing technology, support priorities, and employee needs. Stay engaged and calm when diagnosing unfamiliar or urgent issues. Learn new systems and tools and apply feedback to improve service. Help employees adjust to device, application, and process changes. Collaboration Work closely with other support engineers, IT and Security specialists, and business partners to resolve incidents and deliver consistent support. Share findings and documentation so the team can resolve similar requests more quickly. Coordinate with vendors and other teams when a request crosses support boundaries. Communication Listen carefully, ask clarifying questions, and explain next steps in language suited to each employee. Provide timely updates on open tickets, planned work, outages, and escalations. Write clear ticket notes and communicate respectfully by phone, chat, email, and in person. Strategic Focus Understand how employee technology and responsive support enable Ascendium’s work. Prioritize service based on business impact, urgency, security, and agreed service expectations. Protect employee and company information while following access, device, and change procedures. Build trusted relationships by following through on commitments and seeking feedback. Problem Solving Break down technical problems, test likely causes, and select a practical path to resolution. Use available documentation and tools while knowing when to involve a subject matter expert. Look for patterns in repeat incidents and provide useful evidence for problem management. Verify the solution with the employee and take responsibility for a complete handoff or resolution. Additional Duties As Assigned Knowledge and Skill Requirements A qualified candidate will possess the following. Knowledge equivalent to a degree in information technology or a related field, or comparable practical experience. Three or more years of experience in end-user support, service desk, or deskside support. Working knowledge of computer hardware, operating systems, applications, accounts, and basic networking. Ability to troubleshoot independently and resolve a broad range of employee issues while on the phone or in person. Consistently demonstrates patient, empathetic, and responsive customer service. Ability to organize a ticket queue, assess urgency, follow through, and work with general direction. Clear oral and written communication with employees, IT colleagues, and vendors. Sound judgment, professionalism, curiosity, and a commitment to secure handling of company information. Differentiating Experience A highly qualified candidate will possess any of the following. Experience supporting both Windows and Apple devices in a business environment. Experience with endpoint management, device imaging, patching, and hardware inventory tools. Experience supporting Microsoft 365, identity and access requests, and common collaboration tools. Experience coordinating employee onboarding, offboarding, equipment refreshes, and asset recovery. Experience with IT service management tools, knowledge bases, and service metrics. Experience supporting mobile devices, printers, phones, and meeting room technology. Career advancement, ongoing training, and professional development opportunities. Retirement savings plan with employer match. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. Roles & Responsibilities: MITRE Mission Computing is seeking a Platform Support Engineer to be the front line for the systems that enable critical national security work across MITRE’s Federally Funded Research and Development Centers. You will help users and mission teams get work done on our Kubernetes and cloud platforms: triage issues, author and follow runbooks, escalate when needed, and keep platform teams unblocked. You will be accountable for clear, timely support of the compute environments that power internal tools and the development and production workloads engineering, research, and mission teams depend on. A core part of the job is guiding those teams on how to use the platform and its tools correctly and securely. You will operate in a high-stakes environment defined by novel problems and real constraints, including CMMC compliance, high availability, and cyber resilience. In this environment you will provide the platforms that enable engineering teams of varying skill maturities to deliver innovative solutions and AI-enabled capabilities to MITRE’s U.S. government sponsors. Customer-facing ticket and chat skills: reproduce issues, use runbooks, distinguish application vs. platform problems, escalate clearly, and close work with a usable resolution summary. Participation in incident response and on-call rotations (e.g., PagerDuty), including following escalation paths and documenting what happened. Ability to follow change-management and security procedures in regulated environments (e.g., CMMC, SOC 2). Clear written and verbal communication with users, developers, and platform engineers. Comfort working in a small team with broad ownership, applying documentation and vendor guidance without step-by-step supervision. Experience working in a Kanban workflow: pulling work from a shared board, limiting work in progress, and keeping ticket status current so handoffs stay visible. Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance within one year of hire. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance. This position requires a minimum of 3 days per week on-site in McLean, VA, Bedford, MA, San Diego, CA or Colorado Springs, CO. CompTIA Security+ or CISSP Hands-on use of monitoring and logging tools (e.g., Grafana, Loki, Prometheus, CloudTrail) to find errors and confirm service health. Experience building and supporting CI/CD or Git workflows, including diagnosing pipeline failures, rerunning jobs, and verifying deploy status. Experience supporting and debugging production issues for both Kubernetes users and the platform’s own tool offerings, including collecting logs, events, and workload status. Experience authoring Infrastructure as Code: Terraform that consumes existing modules, and Ansible or similar that use published collections. Familiarity with DNS, certificates, load balancers, and remote access (VPN, bastion, SSH, RDP, WinRM), plus basic connectivity checks (ping, curl, traceroute) to separate network problems from application failures. Experience remediating platform CVEs (e.g., container, EC2, Lambda) and guiding platform users through remediating CVEs in their own workloads. Experience supporting disaster recovery activities: following DR runbooks, performing backup and recovery, and confirming services are back to a known-good state. Prior support work in government, DoD, or other regulated environments. Experience writing platform user guidance, SOPs, runbooks, knowledge-base articles, status updates, and post-mortems. review_candidates.title: Project Coordinator
review_candidates.description: CloudFirst is seeking a highly organized and proactive Project Coordinator to support the successful planning, coordination, and execution of infrastructure, cloud, security, and managed services initiatives across our client portfolio. This role serves as the central coordination point between engineering teams, service delivery, vendors, clients, and leadership to ensure projects remain on schedule, within scope, and aligned with business objectives. The Project Coordinator will help drive delivery consistency, maintain project documentation, track milestones, monitor resource allocation, and provide visibility into project progress and risks. The ideal candidate has strong organizational, communication, and administrative skills, along with experience coordinating IT, cloud, infrastructure, or MSP-related projects in a remote environment. This role reports to Executive Management and Service Leadership and plays a key role in supporting operational efficiency, project accountability, and cross-functional collaboration. Key Responsibilities Project Coordination & Delivery Support · Coordinate infrastructure, cloud, security, and technology projects from initiation through completion. · Assist with developing and maintaining project plans, timelines, milestones, task assignments, and project documentation. · Schedule and facilitate project meetings, ensuring action items, decisions, and follow-ups are documented and tracked. · Monitor project progress and communicate status updates to stakeholders. · Support project managers, engineering teams, and leadership by ensuring deliverables remain on schedule. · Track project dependencies, resource needs, and competing priorities across multiple initiatives. & Operational Support · Maintain project records, documentation, meeting notes, status reports, and decision logs. · Ensure project-related information is organized and accessible to stakeholders. · Assist with tracking project budgets, expenses, time entries, and invoicing coordination. · Support reporting activities using ConnectWise, Microsoft Project, and Microsoft 365 tools. · Coordinate project onboarding activities, resource scheduling, and internal communications. Stakeholder & Vendor Coordination · Serve as a liaison between engineering teams, service delivery, leadership, clients, and vendors. · Follow up on outstanding action items, risks, and project deliverables. · Help ensure clear communication across all project stakeholders. · Coordinate vendor engagements, meetings, project scheduling, and deliverable tracking. Risk Tracking & Quality Assurance · Identify potential project risks, bottlenecks, and scheduling conflicts. · Escalate project concerns and resource constraints to leadership as needed. · Support quality assurance efforts by ensuring project documentation and deliverables meet established standards. · Assist with post-project reviews and lessons learned documentation. CloudFirst-Specific Responsibilities · Support multiple concurrent client projects in a fast-paced Managed Services Provider (MSP) environment. · Coordinate activities between Engineering, Service Desk, and Executive Leadership teams. · Track project milestones, resource utilization, and delivery commitments. · Assist in improving project visibility, reporting, and delivery predictability. · Support compliance, security, and client-specific project requirements. · Maintain leadership reporting and project dashboards. Required Qualifications · 2–5 years of project coordination, project administration, or project management experience. · Experience supporting IT, cloud, infrastructure, cybersecurity, or technology projects. · Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. · Excellent written and verbal communication skills. · Experience with Microsoft 365 applications, including Teams, Outlook, Word, Excel, and SharePoint. · Experience using project management tools such as Microsoft Project, Planner, Asana, Monday.com, Jira, or similar platforms. · Ability to work independently in a fully remote environment. Preferred Qualifications · Experience working within a Managed Services Provider (MSP) environment. · Familiarity with ConnectWise Manage or other Professional Services Automation (PSA) platforms. · Understanding of cloud technologies, Microsoft 365, Azure, networking, cybersecurity, or infrastructure projects. · CAPM, PMP, or other project management certifications are a plus. What We Offer · Fully remote work environment · Competitive compensation · Professional development and growth opportunities · Exposure to enterprise infrastructure, cloud, and cybersecurity projects · Collaborative and supportive team culture · Opportunity to grow into a Project Manager role as the organization expands Experience: ConnectWise: 1 year (Required) Managed Service Provider: 1 year (Required)
